title: Logistics Exception Handling
subtitle: Design an assistant that detects shipment exceptions, drafts resolutions and lets only a narrow, audited set run automatically, with customs always going to a human.
theme: Agents and Copilots in Real Workflows
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Discovery and constraints
practice_prompts.hint: Ask the questions about feeds, approvers, the auto boundary and residency, and say which box each answer moves.

practice_prompts.label: Trace a missed scan
practice_prompts.hint: Follow one webhook and one batch event through detection, the agent, the gate and execution or the queue.

practice_prompts.label: Failures and safe execution
practice_prompts.hint: Explain timeouts, flaky carriers, a missing field and an audit outage, and what the system does for each.

practice_prompts.label: Evaluation and rollout
practice_prompts.hint: Name the release gates, the three rollout stages and how you measure a reroute.

rubric: Places customs first in a gate that is separate from the agent and takes the exception type from detection.
Sizes by event throughput and keeps the model behind cheap detection.
Converges webhook and batch feeds after ingestion and surfaces batch lateness with split time-to-detect.
Uses an idempotency key tied to shipment and resolution version, a circuit breaker with a human fallback, and no action without an audit row.
Keeps EU data in EU data planes, enforced at the application layer as well as storage, and attributes the rule to the customer rather than GDPR.
Raises evaluation unprompted: replay, shadow, staged auto-resolve, zero customs auto-resolves as a release gate and a holdout for reroutes.

editorial_review.evidence: Read all 43 captured sections against the draft. The source repeated the same design four times (interview guide, deep dive, cheat sheet, full design); the walkthrough follows the full design's order (questions, requirements, sizing, architecture, ingestion, gate, residency, reliability, audit, evaluation, trade-offs) and folds the interview-guide and deep-dive versions into the matching step or into a deep dive only where they add mechanism (three timestamps, idempotency key per resolution version, model inputs as regional data, operating metrics). All 16 SVGs are placed as eight light/dark pairs beside the prose that reads them. Added teaching material is labelled illustrative: the $320 Frankfurt parcel, the 0.99-confidence customs trace through both gate orderings, the 3,000-row batch diff and the S:resolution-v1/v2 key trace. The brief opens on the stalled shipment and defines exception, webhook, batch drop, EDI, idempotency key and circuit breaker before use; no approval role was invented beyond the source's ops agents. All 11 Check Yourself questions, 10 follow-ups, the architecture prompt, the two-minute answer and the cost pivot are worked-answer reveals. Source section numbers in moved tables were rewritten to step names. Open items kept explicit: the confidence threshold and shadow agreement target are unspecified in the source. November 20 complete maintained-baseline review: Complete maintained casebook: eleven walkthrough steps, eight protected figures, both feed paths, all gate rules, Frankfurt example, regional topology, execution trace, SAP/weather/manager variant, evaluation and all practice answers. Targeted corrections and source-to-output mappings: /Users/sourav/Github_Repos/Forward-Deployed-Engineer-Interview-Prep/.website_spec/casebook-review-next-ten-2026-11-20/logistics-exception-handling/audit.json. Historical captured-source mappings remain preserved; this pass audits the maintained baseline.
